title: ageratina brevipes
intro: Ageratina brevipes, commonly known as the Mexican angelita, is a flowering plant species native to Mexico and the southwestern United States. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its health benefits, which include reducing inflammation, treating fever, and aiding in the relief of respiratory issues such as coughs and colds. The therapeutic actions of Ageratina brevipes are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which have been shown to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The plant's bioactive compounds have also been found to have potential anti-cancer and neuroprotective effects, making it a subject of ongoing research in the field of pharmacognosy.
